display.purpose: Dashboard h1s and large page headlines. Tight, confident.

body.purpose: All running text, table cells, descriptions, chat bubbles.

label.purpose: KPI labels, sidebar section labels, table column headers, button text.

icon.purpose: Single icon family. Variable font (wght/FILL/GRAD/opsz). Default: wght 400, FILL 0, opsz 24. Not a second typeface — it's a vocabulary of glyphs.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: Resting cards, tables, modals at rest.

shadows.name: pop
shadows.purpose: Hover state on KPI cards and elevated panels.

shadows.name: sidebar
shadows.purpose: Sidebar — single asymmetric shadow in the system.

motion.name: ease-out-quart
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions and the sidebar drawer.

components.name: Primary Button

components.name: Accent Button (Rojo Camarón)
components.description: High-stakes action — Crear ticket, Cerrar, Reabrir. Used sparingly.

components.name: Secondary Button

narrative.northStar: La sala de control de operaciones
narrative.overview: GCM Tickets is the operations nerve center for an internal shrimp-industry workflow. Four roles, one shared ticket lifecycle, every action visible to the people who need it. The visual language reflects that: a quiet, navy-grounded surface, real data on every screen, no decoration that doesn't carry information. The login is cinematic because first impressions of corporate systems earn trust; the in-app surface is calm because the work is dense. We are explicitly not a consumer SaaS. No pastel gradients. No celebratory micro-interactions. The aesthetic is closer to an air-traffic console than a meditation app — the user is operating, not browsing.
keyCharacteristics: Navy-first, not gray-first. The brand color carries identity; surface gray is a quiet canvas for content.
One accent, used with intent. Rojo camarón (#CF301D) is reserved for primary actions, critical status, and the things the user must not miss.
Status communicated three ways. Dot + label + color on every status badge. Color-blind safe by design.
Calm density. Multiple KPIs, tables, and chat surfaces per screen, but a single accent, generous whitespace, no competing gradients.
Spanish, direct, no fluff. Imperative verb buttons. No exclamation marks. No emoji.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Rojo Camarón appears on ≤8% of any given screen, and only on actions the user must not miss. It is never used decoratively.

rules.name: The Ink-Not-Black Rule
rules.body: All text uses brand-ink or a derived slate. Pure black is forbidden; it fights the navy.

rules.name: The Color-Blind Rule
rules.body: Every status is communicated by dot + label + color. Color alone is never the only signal.

rules.name: The Single-Family Rule
rules.body: Inter is the only typeface. No second family, no display serif, no script. Material Symbols is icon vocabulary, not a second typeface.

rules.name: The No-Serif-Display Rule
rules.body: Display headlines stay sans. We are not an editorial; we are an operations console.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadows appear only on hover, focus, or as a response to interaction.

rules.name: The Brand-Tinted Shadow Rule
rules.body: All shadows use rgba(7,29,76, …) not pure black. This is what makes the elevation feel cool and premium.

rules.name: The Consistency Rule
rules.body: Never mix radii inside one component. A button sitting on a 32px card is still 8px; a card inside a 16px surface is still 12px. Mixed-radius compositions are an AI-tell.

rules.name: The Pill Exception
rules.body: Status badges and tag chips use rounded-full (pill). This is the only place pill is allowed. Reaching for rounded-full on a button reaches for a consumer-SaaS tell — stop.

rules.name: The Glass Scope Rule
rules.body: The .login-card translucent surface is the only sanctioned glass surface in the project. Any new surface that wants the same treatment does not get glass — it gets a solid surface with the same brand palette.

rules.name: The Glass Honesty Rule
rules.body: The login card's backdrop-filter is a web approximation of glassmorphism, not Apple Liquid Glass. Comments in styles.css already call this out.

rules.name: The Glass Accessibility Rule
rules.body: Any glass surface must provide a prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce fallback to a solid surface with the same contrast budget. The login card falls back to rgba(7, 29, 76, 0.88).

dos: Do use the brand-navy as the page's primary identity. Sidebar, primary CTAs, and h1s all carry it.
Do use Rojo Camarón for "Create", "Close", "Reopen" and other high-stakes actions. Scarcity is the point.
Do communicate status with dot + label + color. Never color alone.
Do keep surfaces flat at rest. Shadows appear on hover or focus only.
Do cap body line length to 65–75ch on long prose (chat, descriptions).
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion. All animations collapse to instant transitions under that media query.
Do differentiate the four role dashboards. Each role's primary surface reflects its job.
donts: Don't use side-stripe borders (border-left > 1px as a colored accent) on cards, list items, or alerts.
Don't use gradient text. background-clip: text is decorative, never meaningful.

Don't use glassmorphism as a default. Glass is reserved for the login card and nowhere else. Scope: the .login-card is the only sanctioned glass surface — no other surface gets glass. Honesty: the login card is a web approximation of glassmorphism, not Apple Liquid Glass. Accessibility: glass surfaces must fall back to a solid surface under prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce.
Don't ship a hero-metric template (big number + small label + supporting stats + gradient accent) on every screen.
Don't use the same dashboard layout for all four roles.
Don't use celebratory copy or friendly exclamation marks. This is an internal tool.
Don't fabricate hero metrics. The login may feel premium, but every number shown must come from real system state.
Don't use emoji as a UI element. SVG icons and Material Symbols only.
Don't show animation that gates content visibility. Reveals enhance, they don't unlock.
Don't ship a 'small uppercase tracked eyebrow' above every section.
Don't use sidebars with 8+ icon+label sections of identical weight. Three sections maximum.
Don't use zebra tables. Hover state only.
Don't mix radii inside one component. Use 8px on buttons/inputs/chips/sidebar links, 12px on cards/tables/modals, 16px on feature surfaces, 32px on the login card.
Don't reach for rounded-full on buttons. Pill is reserved for status badges and tag chips.
Don't use generic AI tells: 'Get started', 'Welcome back!', sparkles, 'Supercharge your workflow.'
